canonical_statement: For an invertible ergodic probability-preserving transformation and a strongly measurable finite-dimensional real invertible linear cocycle with integrable positive logarithmic norms of the cocycle and its inverse, almost every base point has a finite measurable equivariant direct-sum Lyapunov splitting, and every nonzero vector in each subspace has its assigned asymptotic exponential growth rate.
domain_and_universes: universes u v; probability-measurable Omega : Type u; nonzero finite-dimensional real normed Borel space E : Type v; measurable equivalence T; continuous real-linear equivalence cocycle A
hypotheses: A is strongly measurable as a continuous-linear-map-valued function
conclusion: A LyapunovSplitting T A mu exists. It supplies finitely many strictly ordered exponents and a single strongly measurable family of nonzero complementary equivariant projections whose fixed nonzero vectors have the specified logarithmic growth limit almost everywhere.
degenerate_cases: The fiber has positive finrank. Zero vectors are excluded from the growth clause. Repeated exponent labels are excluded by StrictAnti, while each projected subspace is nonzero and the projections sum to the identity.
